events.title: A Life in Plein Air - New Landscape Paintings by Junyi Ji
events.time: Mon-Fri, 11:00am-5:00pm (or by appointment). (Closed on Sep 7, Labour Day.)
events.location: 4211 No. 3 Road
events.description: A solo exhibition featuring the latest works of accomplished Richmond-based oil painter Junyi Ji. Through masterful technique and a deep connection to nature, Ji captures the beauty of Vancouver’s landscapes, inviting viewers to slow down and rediscover the poetry of the everyday world. Opening Reception & Artist Talk Saturday September 5, 7:00-9:00pm (free event) Lipont Gallery Room 218 (no elevator), 4211 No. 3 Rd Richmond BC Canada V6X 2C3 Free parking on south side of the building only. In an age where digital images can effortlessly reproduce the visible world, artist Junyi Ji advocates for the irreplaceable value of painting from life. Over the past year, Ji has traveled extensively throughout Vancouver and its surrounding areas to document coastlines, forests, parks, city streets and mountains. Working without rehearsal or repetition, every brushstroke responds to a moment that exists only once. “Plein air painting is a dialogue with time,” says Ji. “Each work is created on location, shaped by changing weather, shifting light and the fleeting rhythm of the day. For me, it is not simply an act of copying nature, but a continual process of observation and understanding.” Ji’s paintings seek to capture more than just visual accuracy; they preserve the atmosphere, temperature and emotion of a specific time and place. As sunlight moves across a façade, or the shadows of trees slowly drift, the canvas preserves the quiet presence of Vancouver’s bays, bridges, churches, harbours and cherry blossoms as lived experiences. About Artist Junyi Ji An accomplished oil painter, Junyi Ji holds degrees from the Tianjin Academy of Fine Arts, where he studied under the renowned artist Professor Yu Xiaodong. Known for his superb realistic skills and unique artistic perspective, Ji creates emotionally charged landscapes that capture the diverse beauty of nature through careful detailing and the clever use of colour. Since moving to Canada in 2022, he has established art studios in Richmond and West Vancouver, and to date, has held four solo exhibitions in the Metro Vancouver area. events.location: Main Stage at Surrey Arts Centre 13750 88 Ave
events.description: The Bergmann Duo is delighted to return to Surrey with the captivating programme Fantasies for Two . This special concert showcases some of their favourite works from the piano four-hands repertoire on two pianos. The programme features the magnificent and deeply moving Fantasy in F minor by Franz Schubert, alongside Marcel Bergmann’s own imaginative Fantasy on Gershwin’s Porgy and Bess , inspired by the music of George Gershwin. Get tickets About the Bergmann Duo The Bergmann Duo’s dynamic and energetic performances of uniquely eclectic programmes, which include numerous own arrangements and compositions, have inspired audiences internationally. They have performed in concert and with orchestra in: Canada, the USA, Italy, Germany, The Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, France, Macedonia, Greece and China. The duo has appeared at the: Festival of the Sound, Ottawa International Chamber Music Festival, Abbey Bach Festival,Tuckamore Festival, Ohrid Summer Festival, Zodiac Festival, San Francisco International Music Festival, MusicFest Vancouver, Gilmore International Keyboard Festival, Banff Arts Festival, Royal Bank Calgary International Organ Festival and Competition, Festival Miami, Tage für Neue Musik, Darmstadt, Braunschweiger Kammermusik Podium, and EXPO 2000, Hannover. The married couple received first prize at the International Chamber Music Competition in Caltanissetta, Italy, were laureates of The 4th Murray Dranoff International Two Piano Competition and have performed extensively in Germany as members of the young artists’ roster of Yehudi Menuhin-Live Music Now. The duo studied with Arie Vardi at the Hochschule für Musik und Theater, Hannover and with Jean-Eudes Vaillancourt at the Université de Montréal. events.title: Art Connects: Community Engaged Practice
events.location: Surrey Libraries - City Centre Branch (Room 401), 10350 University Drive, Surrey, BC
events.description: About the event Do you have experience working with the community? Are you curious what this could look like? This event will focus on the joys of welcoming other people into your artistic practice, as well as the ethics and logistics of working with community members. Artists Joan Williams, Mariel Nels, and Carmen Rosen will discuss how they each engage with community to produce artwork and build relationships. No matter what artistic practice you engage in—visual art, performing art, storytelling, photography, etc.—bring your insights and questions; let's talk about what it means to engage with community-led practices! About the speakers Joan Williams is a contemporary Indigenous artist and member of the Semiahmoo First Nation who studied at the Art Institute of Vancouver. Her multidisciplinary practice spans weaving, drawing, and digital arts, blending traditional Coast Salish motifs with modern techniques. Her expansive practice regulary incorporates community engagement. Mariel Nelms works at the intersection of participatory art, visual storytelling, photography, and material exploration. Her practice centers on creating accessible, collaborative art experiences that invite people to engage in making as a way of connecting. Carmen Rosen is an artist, singer, community organizer, and Founding Artistic Director of Still Moon Arts Society. Her creative projects are focused on the Still Creek Watershed in her Renfrew-Collingwood neighbourhood and work within themes of nature, environmental sustainability and the love of working with people and community. What to expect Opportunity to connect with fellow Surrey artists of all disciplines. Meet and interact with community-engaged creatives. Meet City staff from our Civic Theatres and Community Arts teams. Learn about artist opportunities and spaces offered by the City.

events.title: Youth Speak Up Forum
events.location: Surrey City Hall, 13450 104 St, Surrey, BC
events.description: Join us for our annual Youth Speak Up Forum! If you are 13-18, join us at City Hall for a full day of workshops and activities to discuss community topics. You will receive a certificate for participation. Breakfast, lunch, and snacks will also be provided. We will amplify your voice and gather information and recommendations on meaningful topics. This workshop explores what makes people feel welcomed, included, and connected in their community. Youth will share their experiences accessing programs, services, and public spaces, discuss barriers to participation, and provide ideas on how Surrey can strengthen equity, diversity, and inclusion. Participants will help inform efforts that support a more welcoming and accessible city for everyone. Youth Shaping Surrey: Jobs, Business, and Opportunity Led in partnership with Invest Surrey . This workshop focuses on the future of work, business, and economic opportunity in Surrey. Youth will share their perspectives on employment, entrepreneurship, and the types of businesses, services, and amenities they would like to see in their community. Participants will explore ways Surrey can support young entrepreneurs, strengthen career pathways, and create opportunities for youth success. Creating Culture: Youth Shaping Surrey's Arts Scene Led in partnership with the City of Surrey's Community Arts Section. This workshop explores the role of arts, culture, and creativity in building a vibrant city. Youth will share ideas for events, creative spaces, and cultural opportunities, while discussing how Surrey can better support emerging artists, musicians, performers, and creators. Participants will help identify priorities that strengthen Surrey's arts and culture community and make creative opportunities more accessible for young people. City Hall Tour Led by the City of Surrey's Healthy Communities Department. This interactive tour offers youth a behind-the-scenes look at Surrey City Hall and the role local government plays in the community. Participants will learn about City services, meet civic leaders and staff, and explore how young people can contribute ideas, get involved in local initiatives, and help shape the future of Surrey. events.title: Glob
events.location: Main Stage at Surrey Arts Centre 13750 88 Ave Surrey, BC
events.description: "With a global reputation for inventive and visually striking work, Les Foutoukours once again deliver a production that celebrates imagination, beauty and the joy of shared experience." –Theatre Weekly GLOB By Les Foutoukours A whimsical, heart-soothing circus experience where surprises unfold and connection takes centre stage. Two ageless, fluffy beings arrive…waiting for something—anything—to begin. Through hand-to-hand acrobatics, playful juggling and live piano music, they discover time and the magic of simply being. Beautiful, funny, and quietly profound. Drawing on the traditions of silent film comedy, the performance uses physical humour and expressive movement, making the show accessible and welcoming to a wide range of audiences, including Deaf, hard-of-hearing and language-diverse community members. For ages 6+ Get tickets About the artists Performers Rémi Jacques and Jean-Félix Bélanger are part of the creation team of Les Foutoukours of Montreal, Quebec. Les Foutoukours blends storytelling, theatre, clown, dance, and circus to offer entertainment and performances that resonate with people both locally and abroad. Working with talented multidisciplinary artists, this company has distinguished itself in Canada and internationally. Since 1997, Les Foutoukours has produced 20 productions and reached over 500,000 spectators with their intelligent acrobatic clowning.

events.title: Baby SPARK! Little Fox
events.location: Studio Theatre at Surrey Arts Centre, 13750 88 Avenue, Surrey, BC
events.description: Baby SPARK! performances are for babies and their caretakers to enjoy a musical performance together that will spark young imaginations. Enjoy indie-folk vibes with award-winning singer/songwriter and preschool music teacher, Alison Jenkins and violinist Masae Day . Tickets include pre-show refreshments and a post-show stay & play! For children ages 0–2. 10:30–11:00am: Arrive early, settle in, enjoy light refreshments 11:00–11:45am: Musical performance 11:45–12:00pm: Stay & play Get tickets About the artists Led by songwriter/multi-instrumentalist Alison Jenkins , LittleFox is reinventing Chamber Folk, blending roots-y banjo, fiddle, and mandolin with haunting strings, woodwinds, and pedal steel guitar. Since 2021, LittleFox has performed at some of Vancouver's most beloved venues, including The Heatley, The Painted Ship, Water Street Cafe, and Gastown's Guilt & Co. They have also appeared at the White Rock Blues Festival, Khatsahlano Street Party, Galiano Island's Yellowhouse Arts Centre, Gabriola Island's Birdsong house concert series, and are regular performers at Persephone Brewing on the Sunshine Coast. Masae Day is a west coast performer and creator specializing in quirky characters and music-infused performances. Masae plays fiddle with the Vancouver-based indie-folk band LittleFox. She also works with theatre companies across Canada, including the Blyth Festival, Blue Bridge Theatre, Firehall Arts Centre, Axis Theatre, Western Canada Theatre, Thousand Islands Playhouse, Chemainus Theatre Festival, Carousel Theatre For Young People, Seven Tyrants, Ensemble Theatre Company, and Bard On The Beach.
